leaks_found: NEW (A1, narrow): a race between the path rule and the read of the text. resolve_cut accepts LOOK_DECLARED when os.path.realpath(path) is the protocol, and declaration_check then opens `path` again. A symlink re-pointed from the protocol to a harness output between the two (simulated deterministically) gets the look ACCEPTED on proofs.json's text, which quotes the track and the spec sha256. It needs a concurrent process and a symlinked LOOK_DECLARED; the documented command names the protocol directly and cannot be raced this way. No data was read.

NEW (coverage, not on the look's code path): tokenize.open (also used by linecache) and tarfile.open(..., 'r:') call the builtin open they captured at import, so the guard never sees them. Paths it refuses elsewhere (results/holdout/, lab/ CSVs) were not refused (probed on absent paths, nothing read). tarfile's auto-detect mode is refused, through its gzip attempt.

NEW (coverage, analysis only, not demonstrated so as not to touch lab/ inodes): every lab/ path rule (holdout, CSV, lab/data, 2026 names) keys on os.path.realpath, which does not resolve hard links, and /tmp and lab/ are on the same filesystem (/dev/vda). A hard link made outside lab/ to a lab file escapes those rules. It needs os.link inside the process, the same class as os.open / io.FileIO, but it is not listed in the guard's docstring.

Residual, documented, outside the decisions (L4): non-CSV, non-holdout files under lab/ can still be opened and are only recorded. Examples: results/r2/recalc/summary.json, which holds the 2022-2025 validation metrics, and the .pkl/.npy files in lab/audit/scratch. io.FileIO, os.open, io.open_code and pyarrow OSFile / fs files are not covered. For a trades file the guard accepts entry_time < CUT alone, so code other than the harness's own readers (which add exit_time < CUT) could see results realised after the CUT. None of this is on the look's code path: no plugin, no stake rule. Earlier leaks L1, L1b, L2, L3, L4b and L4c are closed (checks 2a-2f).
fixes_needed: Recommended before the declaration (small, vhi_guard.py only; the spec sha256 does not change; re-run proofs.py afterwards): make A1 atomic. In resolve_cut / declaration_check, open DECLARED_PATH (or the resolved path) once. Accept it only if os.fstat(fd) matches os.stat(DECLARED_PATH) on st_dev and st_ino, and read the text from that descriptor. Add the symlink-race probe to proof i.

Recommended (small, look.py plan()): for a look, refuse any CUT other than the end of spec['windows']['look']['eval'] (2026-01-01) before anything is logged, so that a mistyped --cut cannot use up the single access. Today run_spec stops on it only after the access line and the marker are written.
Optional: exit with a non-zero status after writing the output when the check first fails. Today look.py exits 0; the output file and the console are already loud.

Optional (documentation or wraps): re-point tokenize._builtin_open and tarfile.bltn_open as bz2._builtin_open is, or list them in the guard's not-covered list together with hard links. Also note that numpy.fromfile of a path goes through open() in numpy 2.5.
